jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Belize has no AI-specific law, strategy or guidance. Its only binding rule relevant to AI is the right not to be subject to solely automated decisions, including profiling, in the Data Protection Act 2021, which is still awaiting a commencement order. In July 2026 the government announced that it intends to develop a national AI policy.
lead_institutions: Ministry of Public Utilities, Energy, Logistics and E-Governance
narrative.review_notes: This review was carried out on 12 October 2026 from the Attorney General's Ministry law portal. The National Assembly's website is suspended, and the national digital agenda site and the official laws site could not be accessed, so only one document could be read. Belize is marked for a later retry. The planned national AI policy and the national digital agenda are tracked as leads.

instruments.issuing_authority: National Assembly of Belize (House of Representatives and Senate); assented by the Governor-General
instruments.current_status: Enacted as Act No. 45 of 2021 (assent 29 November 2021, gazetted 30 November 2021). Section 97 provides that the Act comes into force on a day appointed by the Minister by Order in the Gazette (different days may be set for different provisions). No commencement order for the Act appeared in the Attorney General's Ministry statutory-instrument listings for 2021-2026 checked on 2026-10-12, so the Act is treated as enacted but not yet in force; the Data Protection Commissioner office it creates has no official sign of being established.
instruments.summary: Belize's general data protection law regulating the collection, keeping, use and dissemination of personal data by data controllers, with GDPR-style principles, data-subject rights and a Data Protection Commissioner as supervisory authority. Section 19 gives data subjects the right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing, including profiling, that produces legal or similarly significant effects, with exceptions for contract, authorising enactments with safeguards, or consent, and requires controllers to inform data subjects of the existence of automated decision-making. Commencement depends on a ministerial order under section 97.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Only binding Belize law with an explicit rule on automated decision-making and profiling (s.19); would govern personal-data processing in AI training and use once in force.
